decisions.finding: Every result (13, 32, 44, 136) uses knowledge I will never have; the one check I can run, called against not-called inside each list, is never shown with numbers.
decisions.reason: Right, but facts cannot supply the exhibit: uplift.policies_call_400 are counts that need both outcomes per advertiser, and there is no called-versus-not-called churn inside any list. The ruling's fallback applies: say plainly the counts are simulation-only. What facts do hold is the same comparison across everyone (uplift.experiment_readout.all_advertisers: 2.9 points, interval 1.8 to 3.9).
decisions.change: Seg 5 opens: 'Only a simulation can count this: it needs both futures for every advertiser. The counts are net, the accounts a call saves minus the few it pushes out', and ends 'You measure it, with the check in the brief.' Seg 8 names 'the check you can run at work' and its card shows the overall readout as the worked form of it.

decisions.finding: A top-400 list split into called and not-called has a margin several times the gap between the uplift and risk lists; the lesson does not say how much randomised data it takes.
decisions.reason: The doubt is correct (noise.margin_of_error_for_a_churn_rate gives +/- 4 points for 250 advertisers at a 12 percent rate, wider at list-top rates; the lists differ by 12 churns in 400). Facts give the amount of randomised data (all 12,000 advertisers) but not the interval inside each list, so that part is said without a figure.
decisions.change: Seg 8: 'Split 400 names in two and it is several points wide, enough to swallow the whole effect, so pool several rounds before ranking one list above another.' Seg 4 card: 'decides who gets the call (here: all 12,000 advertisers)'. Seg 8 card: 'expect several points either way'.
